review_notes: Read the whole target file, which contains two theorems and has no simp lemmas of its own. I checked the simp status of the lemmas it relies on. `coeff_restrictedResidue` and `coeff_restrictedResidueHom` are already @[simp]. `coeff_polynomialRestrictedFinFirst` (FirstVariableRegrouping/Fin.lean) is not simp. The same manual rw/simp-only pattern appears here and in FirstVariableDivision.lean. I did not run Lean. I did not check whether other unrelated lemmas would interfere with the proposed simp lemma. I did not check whether `Subring.coe_zero` and `coeff_zero` fire as expected.

findings.problem: `coeff_polynomialRestrictedFinFirst` is the canonical coefficient-extraction rule for `polynomialRestrictedFinFirst`, but it is not tagged @[simp]. Each proof has to `rw` it by hand, then prove `R.coeff i = 0` separately, then call `simp only [hzero, Subring.coe_zero, coeff_zero]`. The same three-step pattern appears at FirstVariableDivision.lean lines 95-98 and 162-165. The expression `coeff (β.cons i) (polynomialRestrictedFinFirst I n P)` has no simp normal form, so `simp` cannot reduce it to the coefficient `coeff β (P.coeff i)` on the Fin n side.
findings.proposed_change: Mark `coeff_polynomialRestrictedFinFirst` with `@[simp]` in FirstVariableRegrouping/Fin.lean. It rewrites an image coefficient to a strictly smaller expression, with no cycle. Then each vanishing-coefficient block can reduce to `intro i β hi; simp [(Polynomial.degree_lt_iff_coeff_zero R d).mp hRdegree i hi]`. Alternatively, factor the repeated block into one lemma, such as one stating that the coefficients of `polynomialRestrictedFinFirst I n P` vanish at `β.cons i` for `i ≥ d` when `P.degree < d`, and use that lemma here and in FirstVariableDivision.
findings.benefit: The repeated rw/have/simp-only boilerplate shrinks. Later proofs about `polynomialRestrictedFinFirst` coefficients can use plain `simp`, and the normal form is the more elementary `Fin n` coefficient `coeff β (P.coeff i)`.
